mainTopic: שיעורים for carrying seeds, locusts, pits, and hairs; the end of פרק אמר רבי עקיבא and the opening משנה of פרק המצניע (שבת צ:)
overview: The משנה finishes its list of minimum amounts (שיעורים) for carrying out (הוצאה) on שבת. Garden seeds need two. A live kosher locust and the special locust צפורת כרמים count at any amount, and רבי יהודה adds a live non-kosher locust, because people keep it as a toy for a child. The גמרא asks why seeds need two when one plant's worth of fertilizer counts. רב פפא answers that nobody plants just one seed. Two ברייתות then list amounts for date pits, which depend on their use, and for animal hairs and palm fibers. רב identifies צפורת כרמים, and אביי describes how it was used as a charm for wisdom. The גמרא explains that the תנא קמא worries a non-kosher locust will die and the child will eat it, while רבי יהודה says the child would mourn it instead. After the הדרן, a new chapter opens with the rule that one who stored an item for a purpose is liable for carrying any amount. אביי explains that the case is someone who forgot why he stored it.

steps.title: משנה: Garden seeds need two
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that carrying out cucumber, squash, or Egyptian bean seeds makes one liable only if he carries two seeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Cucumber seeds — two. Squash seeds — two. Egyptian bean seeds — two.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of minimum amounts for הוצאה. For these three kinds of garden seeds, the minimum is two seeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liability for carrying depends on whether the item is a 'significant amount' that a person would bother with. These seeds are large, so a small number already counts. Still, the minimum is two and not one, and the גמרא will soon explain why.

phrases.english: Cucumber seeds — two.
Squash seeds — two.
Egyptian bean seeds — two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of שיעורים from the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For cucumber, squash, and Egyptian bean seeds, the שיעור for הוצאה is two seeds.

steps.title: משנה: Locusts, live and dead, and the special vineyard locust
steps.stepSummary: A live kosher locust: any amount. A dead one: a dried fig's volume, like other food. צפורת כרמים, live or dead: any amount, because people store it for medicine.
steps.simpleTranslation: A live kosher locust — any amount. A dead one — a dried fig's volume. The vineyard locust (צפורת כרמים), whether alive or dead — any amount, because people store it for medicine.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the amounts for locusts. The amount depends on how people use each kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A live kosher locust counts at any amount because people keep it as a toy for a child. This is the reason רבי יהודה's 'אף' extends to the non-kosher one, and the reason the גמרא later discusses giving a kosher locust to a child. A dead kosher locust is just food, so it follows the normal food amount of a כגרוגרת. צפורת כרמים is kept for healing, so even a tiny one is significant, alive or dead.

keyTerms.meaning: The volume of a dried fig (the standard food amount for carrying)
A type of locust found in vineyards
People store / put away (it is considered valuable)

steps.confusionAlert: Even though צפורת כרמים has the word 'bird' (צפור) in it, it is a type of locust, not a bird.

phrases.english: A live kosher locust — any amount.
A dead one — a dried fig's volume.
The vineyard locust,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין חַיָּה בֵּין מֵתָה — כׇּל שֶׁהוּא,
phrases.english: whether alive or dead — any amount,
because people store it for medicine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list with a new category, locusts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Live kosher locust: any amount. Dead kosher locust: כגרוגרת. צפורת כרמים: any amount, since it is stored for medicine.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: A live non-kosher locust also counts at any amount
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה adds that carrying even a live non-kosher locust makes one liable at any amount, because people keep it as a toy for a child.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Even one who carries out a live non-kosher locust is liable for any amount, because people store it for a child to play with.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds one more case to the 'any amount' list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא already agrees that a live kosher locust counts at any amount because children play with it. רבי יהודה says the same is true of a live non-kosher locust. The תנא קמא disagrees only because he holds that people do not give a non-kosher locust to a child. The גמרא explains his reason in steps 14-20.

keyTerms.meaning: Non-kosher (here: a forbidden species of locust)

steps.whatToRemember: Throughout this משנה, the minimum amount depends on how people actually use and value the item.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אַף הַמּוֹצִיא חָגָב חַי טָמֵא כׇּל שֶׁהוּא,
phrases.english: Even one who carries out a live non-kosher locust — any amount,
because people store it for a child to play with.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף הַמּוֹצִיא חָגָב חַי טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a dissenting expansion to the locust rulings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a live non-kosher locust is significant at any amount because it is kept as a child's toy.

steps.title: Contradiction from the amount of fertilizer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה from earlier in the מסכת: the amount of fertilizer that counts is enough for one plant (one cabbage stalk or one leek). So why do seeds need two?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: They contrasted it: Compost and fine sand — enough to fertilize one cabbage stalk, says רבי עקיבא. The חכמים say: enough to fertilize one leek!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule of 'two seeds.' Another source says one plant is enough to count when it comes to fertilizer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If fertilizing a single plant is significant, then planting a single seed should also be significant. So the minimum for seeds should be one, not two. רבי עקיבא and the חכמים argue only about which plant, but both agree that one plant counts.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction (two sources seem to clash)

phrases.english: GEMARA: And they contrasted it:
Compost and fine sand —
enough to fertilize a cabbage stalk,
the words of Rabbi Akiva.
And the Sages say: enough to fertilize a leek!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'two seeds' ruling in step 1 using an earlier משנה about fertilizer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that seeds require two to be liable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The fertilizer משנה treats one plant's worth as significant, so one seed (one plant) should also be significant.

steps.title: רב פפא: Planted plants versus unplanted seeds
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that fertilizer is for a plant already growing, and one plant is worth fertilizing. Seeds are for planting, and nobody bothers to plant just one seed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This (fertilizer) is for something already planted; that (seeds) is for something not yet planted — because a person does not bother to carry out a single seed for planting.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא resolves the contradiction by explaining that the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a plant that is already growing, people do care for even one plant, so one plant's worth of fertilizer counts. When planting from scratch, people always plant several seeds, so a single seed is not significant. That is why the minimum is two.
steps.whatToRemember: The שיעור follows normal human behavior: people tend one existing plant, but they never plant just one seed.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
This is where it is planted, that is where it is not planted —
because a person does not take the trouble
to carry out a single seed for planting.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הָא דִּזְרִיעַ, הָא דְּלָא זְרִיעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases (אוקימתא: the two sources speak of different situations)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Fertilizer for one plant counts, so one seed should count too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Fertilizer serves an existing plant, where one plant matters. Seeds are for new planting, where nobody plants just one.

steps.title: ברייתא: Date pits measured by their intended use
steps.stepSummary: Starting from the משנה's 'cucumber seeds,' the גמרא brings a ברייתא: date pits for planting — two; for animal food — one (a pig's mouthful); for fuel — enough to cook a light egg.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Cucumber seeds.' The רבנן taught: One who carries out pits — if for planting, two; if for eating, a pig's mouthful, and how much is a pig's mouthful? One. If for fuel, enough to cook a light egg.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that expands on the משנה's seed rule. The minimum for date pits changes depending on what the person plans to use them for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same object can have different minimums. For planting it is two, matching רב פפא's idea that nobody plants just one. A pig will eat even a single pit, so for food it is one. For fuel, the measure is how much heat is needed to cook a small egg.

phrases.english: 'Cucumber seeds.'
phrases.notes: Quotes the משנה as a heading for the new discussion.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: One who carries out pits,
if for planting — two,
if for eating — a pig's mouthful,
and how much is a pig's mouthful? One.

phrases.aramaic: אִם לְהַסִּיק — כְּדֵי לְבַשֵּׁל בֵּיצָה קַלָּה.
phrases.english: If for burning — enough to cook a light egg.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶרַע קִישּׁוּאִין. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַמּוֹצִיא גַּרְעִינִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's seed clause and brings a related ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For date pits, the שיעור depends on purpose: planting — two; food — one; fuel — enough to cook a light egg.

steps.title: Pits used for counting: two or five
steps.stepSummary: If the pits are carried out for counting, the ברייתא says two. אחרים say five.
steps.simpleTranslation: If for counting — two. אחרים say: five.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds one more use, counting, and brings a disagreement about its amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view holds that two pits are already a useful counting aid. אחרים hold that a person can count up to five in his head, so pits matter only once there are five.

phrases.english: If for counting — two.
Others say: five.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם לְחֶשְׁבּוֹן — שְׁתַּיִם. אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים: חָמֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a fourth use and a dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pits carried for counting: two according to the first view, five according to אחרים.
steps.whatToRemember: The same item can have several different שיעורים. It all depends on the use the person intends.

steps.title: ברייתא: Hairs and palm fibers
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules: two hairs from a horse's or cow's tail make one liable, because they are kept for traps. One stiff pig bristle counts. Palm fronds need two, and thin palm fibers need one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One who carries out two hairs from a horse's tail or a cow's tail is liable, because people store them for traps. A pig's bristle — one. Palm fronds — two. Palm fibers — one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא listing the minimum amounts for small things that people save for practical uses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each amount reflects a real use. Tail hairs are kept for making snares. A stiff pig bristle is used as a needle for sewing leather, so even one is useful. The fronds and fibers differ because of how much of each is needed.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: One who carries out two hairs
from a horse's tail or from a cow's tail — is liable,
because people store them for traps.
A stiff pig bristle — one.
Palm fronds — two.
Palm fibers — one.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַמּוֹצִיא שְׁנֵי נִימִין מִזְּנַב הַסּוּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel ברייתא of small-item שיעורים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Horse or cow tail hairs: two. Pig bristle: one. Palm fronds: two. Palm fibers: one.

steps.title: What is the vineyard locust?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about צפורת כרמים and asks what this creature is.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The vineyard locust, whether alive or dead — any amount.' What is the vineyard locust?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה's line about צפורת כרמים and asks what exactly it is. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה used an unfamiliar name. Before discussing it further, the גמרא needs to identify the creature.

phrases.english: 'The vineyard locust,'

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין חַיָּה בֵּין מֵתָה — כׇּל שֶׁהוּא.
phrases.english: whether alive or dead — any amount.'
What is the vineyard locust?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to a later clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the creature called צפורת כרמים.

steps.title: רב: It is the פליא ביארי
steps.stepSummary: רב identifies צפורת כרמים as a locust known as פליא ביארי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: It is the פליא ביארי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question by giving the creature's common local name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב matches the משנה's term to a locust that people in his time knew by name. That makes the creature identifiable.

keyTerms.meaning: The local name of this locust

phrases.english: Rav said: palya biari.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: צפורת כרמים is the locust called פליא ביארי.

steps.title: אביי: Where it is found and its use for wisdom
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds that it is found on a palm tree with a single shoot, and people use it as a charm for wisdom.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: And it is found on a palm tree that has one shoot, and people use it for wisdom.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds details about where the locust is found and what people do with it. This sets up his description of the procedure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains the משנה's reason that it is 'stored for healing': it was used as a charm. Because it has a valued use, even one counts for liability.

keyTerms.meaning: A shoot / vine of a palm

phrases.english: Abaye said:
And it is found on a palm tree with a single shoot,
and people use it for wisdom.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: וּמִשְׁתַּכְחָא בְּדִיקְלָא דְּחַד נְבָארָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to רב's identification.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The locust lives on single-shoot palms and is used as a charm for wisdom.

steps.title: How the charm was used, with a verse to remember it
steps.stepSummary: One eats the right half and seals the left half in a copper tube with sixty seals, then hangs it on the left arm. The verse 'a wise heart is to his right' reminds you which half is which.
steps.simpleTranslation: He eats its right half, puts its left half into a copper tube, seals it with sixty seals, and hangs it on his left arm. Your memory aid: 'A wise man's heart is to his right, and a fool's heart is to his left.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי describes the steps of the wisdom charm and gives a verse to help remember which half to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The right half is the 'wisdom' side, so it is eaten. The left half is preserved on the arm. The verse from קהלת links 'right' with wisdom, so you will not mix up the halves.

phrases.english: He eats its right half,

phrases.aramaic: וּפַלְגָא דִשְׂמָאלֵיהּ רָמֵי לֵהּ בְּגוּבְתָּא דִנְחָשָׁא
phrases.english: and its left half he places in a copper tube
and seals it with sixty seals,
and hangs it on his left arm.
And your mnemonic:
'A wise man's heart is to his right, and a fool's heart to his left' (Ecclesiastes 10:2),

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's description with the procedure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eat the right half; seal the left half in a copper tube and wear it on the left arm.

steps.title: Learning as much as you want, then eating the other half
steps.stepSummary: The person then gains wisdom and learns as much as he wants. Afterward he must eat the other half, or else his learning will be forgotten.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he grows wise as much as he wants, and learns as much as he wants, and then eats the other half — for if not, his learning will be uprooted.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes describing the charm: what it does and the final step needed so the learning stays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The charm brings wisdom, but at the end the second half must also be eaten. Otherwise the learning will be lost. This shows how valuable this locust was considered, which explains why even one makes a person liable for carrying it.
steps.whatToRemember: צפורת כרמים was highly valued as a charm for wisdom. That is why the משנה makes a person liable for carrying even the smallest amount of it.

phrases.english: and he grows wise as much as he wants,
and learns as much as he wants,
and eats the other half,
for if not — his learning is uprooted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's description of the charm.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The charm grants wisdom, but the second half must also be eaten at the end to keep the learning. This explains why צפורת כרמים is significant in any amount.

steps.title: Quoting רבי יהודה's view on the live non-kosher locust
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה from the משנה and notes that the תנא קמא disagrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Even one who carries out (a live non-kosher locust is liable for any amount, because people store it for a child to play with). And the תנא קמא holds: no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes רבי יהודה, who says a live non-kosher locust counts even in a tiny amount because people keep it as a toy for a child. This line sets up the next move: figuring out why the תנא קמא disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's point is that people actually store such a locust for children, so carrying any amount makes one liable. The תנא קמא says people do not give a non-kosher locust to a child to play with. So the dispute is about real-world behavior, and the גמרא will now look for the reason behind the תנא קמא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה
Etc.: the rest of the quote is understood

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says
Even one who carries out, etc.
phrases.notes: The full משנה: a live non-kosher locust, any amount, because people store it for a child to play with

phrases.english: And the first tanna holds: no.
phrases.notes: People do not give a non-kosher locust to a child as a toy

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the צפורת כרמים discussion to the next clause of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: carrying a live טמא locust makes one liable for any amount, because it is stored for children. The תנא קמא disagrees.

steps.title: Why does the first opinion disagree?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the תנא קמא's position.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the תנא קמא thinks people would not give a non-kosher locust to a child to play with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simple request for the reasoning behind the view. It sets up an answer that will be tested and then replaced.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the תנא קמא's view quoted in Step 14
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the תנא קמא holds that people do not give a non-kosher locust to a child

steps.title: First answer: the child might eat it
steps.stepSummary: The proposed reason is the worry that the child will eat the non-kosher locust.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps the child will eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that parents would not give a non-kosher locust to a child because the child might eat it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating a non-kosher locust is forbidden. So if a child might eat his toy, parents would avoid giving it. That would mean people do not store it for children, which supports the תנא קמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps; there is a worry that

phrases.english: Perhaps he will eat it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The child might eat the non-kosher locust

steps.title: Challenge: then a kosher locust should be a problem too
steps.stepSummary: If the worry is eating, the same worry should apply to a kosher locust.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a kosher locust too (should not be given to a child, because he might eat it).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first answer. If we are afraid the child will eat the locust, that fear applies to a kosher locust too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumes that eating even a kosher locust while it is alive is forbidden. The next step proves this from a story. So 'he might eat it' cannot be what separates a טמא locust from a טהור one.

phrases.english: If so, a kosher one too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason 'perhaps he will eat it'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Eating a live kosher locust is also forbidden, so the worry would make a kosher locust a problem as well. It therefore does not explain why only the non-kosher one is excluded.

steps.title: Proof: רב warned רב כהנא about a live kosher locust
steps.stepSummary: A story shows that eating a live kosher locust is forbidden under בל תשקצו.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב כהנא was standing before רב, and he was passing a kosher locust near his mouth. רב said to him: Take it away, so people will not say he is eating it and violating 'Do not make yourselves detestable'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its challenge with a story. רב told רב כהנא to move a live kosher locust away from his mouth so people would not think he was eating it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's warning shows that eating a live kosher locust violates בל תשקצו. So a kosher locust given to a child carries the same 'he might eat it' risk. That makes the first answer fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition 'Do not make yourselves detestable' (eating repulsive things)

steps.confusionAlert: רב כהנא was not actually eating the locust. רב's concern was only how it looked to others. The story still proves that really eating a live locust is forbidden.

phrases.english: For Rav Kahana
was standing before Rav,
and he was passing a kosher locust over his mouth.
He said to him: Take it away,
so that they will not say he is eating it,
and is violating the prohibition of
'You shall not make yourselves detestable'!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָא רַב כָּהֲנָא הֲוָה קָאֵים קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the challenge of Step 17
steps.raayaObject: That eating a live kosher locust is forbidden, so 'he might eat it' applies to a kosher locust too
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's instruction to רב כהנא, based on בל תשקצו

steps.title: New reason: it might die and then he will eat it
steps.stepSummary: The real worry of the תנא קמא is that the locust will die and the child will eat the non-kosher carcass.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, (the worry is) perhaps it will die and he will eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the first answer and gives a new one. The concern is that the non-kosher locust might die and then the child might eat it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is no longer that the child will eat the live locust. It is that the locust will die and then be eaten. If a kosher locust dies, eating it is permitted, so there is no problem. If a non-kosher locust dies, the child would be eating forbidden food. So this worry applies only to the טמא locust.

phrases.english: Rather,
perhaps it will die and he will eat it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of Step 16 after the challenge of Steps 17-18
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The worry was that the child would eat the live locust
steps.terutzMaskana: The worry is that the non-kosher locust will die and the child will eat its carcass

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a child would mourn it, not eat it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rejects the worry, because a child would mourn his dead pet rather than eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה (holds): if it dies, the child will eulogize it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יהודה is not worried. A child who loses his pet locust will cry over it, not eat it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This finishes explaining the dispute. Both opinions agree on the facts about what is forbidden. They disagree only about how a child would act once the locust dies.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא worries that a dead non-kosher locust could be eaten by the child. רבי יהודה says a child mourns his dead pet, so people do store such a locust for children.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda (holds):
if it dies,
the child will surely eulogize it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of Step 19 by giving רבי יהודה's side
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dispute depends on whether a child would eat a dead non-kosher locust (תנא קמא) or mourn it (רבי יהודה).

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק אמר רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the chapter אמר רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, אמר רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the chapter אמר רבי עקיבא. A new chapter begins next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional farewell said when a chapter is finished. It expresses the hope of coming back to learn it again. It adds no new law.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: the closing formula of a פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you,
(chapter) 'Rabbi Akiva said'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final discussion in Steps 14-20
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: End of פרק אמר רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: New משנה: carrying something one stored for a purpose
steps.stepSummary: Someone who stored an item for sowing, as a sample, or for medicine is liable for carrying any amount. Others need the normal minimum, and bringing it back in also needs the normal minimum.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who stores (something) for sowing, as a sample, or for medicine, and carried it out on שבת, is liable for any amount. Any other person is only liable for its standard measure. If he went back and brought it in, he is only liable for its standard measure.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter opens with a משנה. If you specially stored a small item for a use, carrying even a tiny bit of it makes you liable, but other people need the usual minimum amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally carrying is only forbidden by תורה law if you carry a significant amount, the שיעור. By storing it, this person showed that even a tiny amount matters to him, so it counts for him. Other people have not shown this, and bringing it back in without that purpose also falls back to the normal שיעור.

keyTerms.meaning: One who stores something away (showing it matters to him)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key rule of הוצאה: a person's own intent can make a small amount significant, but only for him.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who stores (something) for sowing
or as a sample or for medicine
and carried it out on Shabbat
is liable for any amount.
And any (other) person
is liable for it only at its standard measure.
If he went back and brought it in,
he is liable only at its standard measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new chapter המצניע after the הדרן of Step 21
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who stored an item for a purpose is liable for carrying any amount. Others, and bringing it back in, require the standard שיעור.

steps.title: Why does the משנה say 'stores' instead of 'carries out'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה mentions storing. It could have simply said 'one who carries out for sowing'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does it need to teach 'one who stores'? Let it teach: 'one who carries out for sowing, as a sample, or for medicine is liable for any amount'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the wording of the משנה. Why mention storing at all, when carrying out for one of these purposes should be enough to make him liable?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liability comes from the act of carrying, not from storing. And carrying with a clear purpose already shows the small amount matters to him. So the word 'stores' looks unnecessary, and the גמרא wants to know what it adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does it need to teach?

phrases.english: GEMARA: Why does he need
to teach 'one who stores'?
Let it teach: one who carries out
for sowing, or as a sample, or for medicine
is liable for any amount!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the משנה in Step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: The word הַמַּצְנִיעַ in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Carrying out for a stated purpose should be enough to make him liable for any amount, so mentioning storage seems unnecessary.

steps.title: אביי: he forgot why he stored it
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains the case: he stored it, forgot why, and now carries it out with no specific purpose. The earlier storing is what makes him liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: What case are we dealing with here? Where he stored it and forgot why he stored it, and now he carries it out with no specific purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that the משנה is talking about a person who carries the item out with no plan, because he forgot why he saved it. Only his earlier storing shows that it mattered to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he carried it out for a clear use, 'one who carries out' would have been enough. Here his current carrying has no purpose. The משנה therefore teaches that the earlier act of storing still makes the small amount significant, so he is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (introduces a specific case)

steps.whatToRemember: The word 'stores' teaches that the earlier storing alone makes a tiny amount count, even if he now carries it out with no purpose because he forgot why he saved it.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
With what are we dealing here?
For example, where he stored it
and forgot why he stored it,
and now he carries it out with no specific purpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of Step 23
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'stores' is unnecessary, because carrying for a purpose already makes one liable
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is where he forgot why he stored it and carries it out with no purpose, so liability comes only from the earlier storing
